links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and misdiagnosis rate with versus without a 90% confidence threshold
links.effect: Baseline top-diagnosis accuracy 55.1%, misdiagnosis 29.4%. With 90% confidence threshold, accuracy 72.9%, five-candidate applicability 85.9%, misdiagnoses 14.1%, but only half of cases analyzed.
links.quote: Applying a 90% confidence threshold increased the accuracy of the top diagnosis to 72.9% and the applicability of the five candidates to 85.9%, while reducing misdiagnoses to 14.1%, but limited the analysis to half of cases.

links.outcome: Whether confidence-based deferral reduces misdiagnosis while limiting cases analyzed
links.effect: 90% confidence threshold reduced misdiagnoses from 29.4% to 14.1% and raised top-diagnosis accuracy to 72.9%, but restricted analysis to half of cases.
links.quote: Applying a 90% confidence threshold increased the accuracy of the top diagnosis to 72.9% and the applicability of the five candidates to 85.9%, while reducing misdiagnoses to 14.1%, but limited the analysis to half of cases.
